title: WPSS/1672/2013 of Smt Pushpa Joshi Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPSS No.1672 of 2013
Honíble V.K. Bist, J.
Mr. K.N. Joshi, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. Rakesh Kumar Joshi, Brief
Holder for the State.
Heard learned counsel for the
parties.
On 17.06.2013, the petitioner was
transferred from Government Upper
Primary School, Fagpur to Government
Upper Primary School, Budham, district
Champawat. Since there was no post
available in Government Upper Primary
School, Budham, the Block Education
Officer, Champawat invited options from
the petitioner. She submitted her options
and thereafter, an order was passed on
14.09.2013, amending the order dated
17.06.2013, by which the petitioner was
transferred from Government Upper
Primary School, Fagpur to Government
Upper Primary School, Khirdwari, district
Champawat. In Government Upper
Primary School, Khirdwari, district
Champawat also, there was no post
vacant. Thereafter, on 30.09.2013 an
order was passed by which the petitioner
has been transferred from Government
Upper Primary School, Fagpur to
Government Upper Primary School, Need,
district Champawat. Against the said
transfer order, present petition has been
filed by the petitioner.
The petitioner has annexed a
document (downloaded from the website of
Education Department) issued by the
department, in which it is shown that no

post is lying vacant in the Upper Primary
School, Need.
The contention of the learned counsel
for the petitioner is that the petitioner
cannot be transferred to a place where the
post is not vacant. Learned counsel for the
petitioner argued that the respondents are
acting in discriminatory manner; as in
other cases, they have stayed the transfer
orders of those employees whose names
were mentioned in the earlier transfer
order; as there was no post vacant. He
argued that the post from where the
petitioner has been transferred is still
vacant and if, the case of the petitioner is
considered in proper manner and the
petitioner is permitted to work at the
present place of posting, no harm will be
caused to anybody and in fact, it will be in
the interest of the students. He also
argued that the petitioner has already
worked in the Durgam area, but the
respondents, while passing the order
impugned, have not considered this fact.
He submitted that the petitioner is also
suffering from low back pain and is
undergoing treatment from Bareilly and
she is not in a position to serve at a
remote place.
Mr. Rakesh Kumar Joshi, Brief
Holder for the State submitted that the
petitioner is working at the present place
of posting since 1998 and as per the
Transfer Rules, she has to be transferred
to another place; as she has completed
more than three years in one place of
posting. He submitted that there is
provision under Rule 26 of the Transfer

rules under which the petitioner can file
appeal.
Considering the submission
advanced by the learned counsel for the
parties, the writ petition is disposed of by
permitting the petitioner to submit a
representation before the competent
authority within one week. In case such
representation is filed by the petitioner
within the stipulated period, the
competent authority shall take decision on
the representation of the petitioner, in
accordance with law, within a period of ten
daysí from the date of filing of
representation along with the certified
copy of this order. Till the representation
filed by the petitioner is decided, the order
impugned (so far it relates to the
petitioner), shall be kept in abeyance.
Stay application also stands disposed
of.
No order as to costs.
Let a certified copy of this order be
supplied to the learned counsel for the
parties today itself on payment of usual
charges.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
Arpan 24.10.2013
